column2: Fry the onion in olive oil for 3 minutes; add the vegetables and sauté for 5 minutes.
Add the tomato paste and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the bulgur and chickpeas and toast for 2 minutes.
Add the hot water and salt; once boiling, cook covered over low heat for 15 minutes until absorbed.
Add the butter, put a paper towel under the lid and let rest for 10 minutes.
If using eggplant, soak it in salted water for 15 minutes first to remove the bitterness.
The resting time keeps the grains separate.
Serve with cacık or yogurt.
Wholewheat pasta with vegetable sauce
350 g wholewheat penne or fusilli
2 cups diced vegetables (zucchini, eggplant, broccoli, mushroom, spinach, celeriac or carrot)
2 grated tomatoes
Bring plenty of salted water to the boil; cook the pasta for the time on the packet and reserve 1 cup of cooking water before draining.
Meanwhile, fry the onion in olive oil for 3 minutes, then the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the vegetables and sauté for 6–8 minutes until soft (spinach needs only 2 minutes).
Add the tomato, salt and chilli flakes and cook for 5 minutes until thickened.
Add the pasta to the sauce; mix for 1 minute, adding some of the reserved cooking water if needed.
Sprinkle with cheese and serve immediately.
The starch in the cooking water helps the sauce cling to the pasta.
Wholewheat pasta takes 1–2 minutes longer than white pasta.
Serve hot with yogurt or a green salad on the side.
Keeps for 2 days in the fridge; add 2 spoons of water when reheating.
Chicken and eggplant tray bake
2 eggplants (large cubes)
500 g boneless chicken thighs (large cubes)
1 onion (coarsely chopped)
2 tomatoes (diced)
Peel the eggplants in stripes and dice; soak in salted water for 15 minutes, drain and pat dry.
Toss the chicken, eggplant, potato, onion and pepper in a large bowl with olive oil, paprika, thyme and salt.
Spread the mixture in a single layer on a baking tray; scatter the tomatoes in between.
Dissolve the tomato paste in hot water, drizzle over the tray, cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake for another 15 minutes until golden on top and the potatoes are soft.
Soaking eggplant in salted water removes bitterness and makes it absorb less oil.
Serve hot with cacık or yogurt.
Spiced chicken and cauliflower tray bake
500 g boneless chicken thighs
1 red onion (sliced)
Half a teaspoon turmeric
Mix the yogurt, 1 tablespoon olive oil, paprika, cumin, turmeric, garlic and half a teaspoon salt and marinate the chicken in it for 20 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 210 °C.
Toss the cauliflower and onion with the remaining olive oil and salt and spread on the tray.
Place the chicken among the cauliflower.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until the cauliflower is golden at the edges and the chicken is fully cooked.
Squeeze lemon over and serve.
A yogurt marinade tenderises the chicken; you can leave it in the fridge for up to 4 hours.
Serve with bulgur pilaf or lavash.
Baked salmon on a bed of vegetables
4 salmon steaks
3 cups chopped vegetables (cauliflower, broccoli, leek, celeriac or carrot)
Toss the vegetables with 2 tablespoons olive oil, thyme and half the salt.
Spread on the tray and pre-bake for 12 minutes.
Place the salmon on the vegetables and brush with the remaining oil, salt and lemon juice.
Bake for 12–14 minutes until the salmon is opaque.
Pre-cooking the vegetables means the salmon is ready without drying out.
Hot, with lemon slices.
Roasted vegetable tahini meze
500 g vegetables (eggplant, zucchini, cauliflower, celeriac, carrot or broccoli)
Preheat the oven to 220 °C. Prick the whole eggplant with a fork; coarsely chop the other vegetables.
Toss the vegetables with 1 tablespoon olive oil and spread on the tray.
Roast for 25–30 minutes until charred at the edges and soft inside; peel the eggplant.
Finely chop the vegetables with a knife or mash with a fork and leave to cool.
Whisk the tahini, yogurt, garlic, lemon juice and salt; mix with the vegetables.
Spread on a plate and garnish with the remaining olive oil and chopped parsley.
If the tahini thickens, thin it with 1–2 spoons of cold water.
If you add yogurt before the vegetables have cooled completely, the meze turns watery.
Serve cold with lavash or toasted bread.
Keeps for 3 days in a closed container in the fridge.
Baked fruit and oat dessert
4 cups sliced fruit (apple, pear, peach, apricot, plum, sour cherry, blackberry or blueberry)
2 tablespoons brown sugar
Half a cup wholewheat flour
4 tablespoons cold butter
3 tablespoons honey
Half a cup coarsely chopped walnuts
Preheat the oven to 180 °C; butter a 20×25 cm baking dish.
Toss the fruit with lemon juice, brown sugar and half the cinnamon and spread in the dish.
Mix the oats, flour and remaining cinnamon; add the cold butter and rub with your fingertips until it looks like coarse sand.
Add the honey and walnuts and mix; sprinkle these crumbs evenly over the fruit.
Bake for 35 minutes until golden on top and the fruit juices bubble at the edges.
Let rest for 15 minutes and serve.
With juicy fruit (sour cherry, blackberry), mix 1 tablespoon starch into the fruit so the dessert holds together better.
The butter must be cold or the crumbs won’t turn crisp.
Serve lukewarm with a scoop of ice cream or a spoonful of strained yogurt.
Keeps for 1 day at room temperature and 3 days in the fridge; warm in the oven for 10 minutes.
Chilled fruit and yogurt cups
2 cups seasonal fruit (apple, pear, banana, peach, apricot, strawberry, sour cherry or blueberry)
4 tablespoons rolled oats
2 tablespoons coarsely chopped walnuts
Wash the fruit; dice apple and pear, slice banana into rounds and quarter strawberries. Pit the sour cherries.
Soften firm fruit (apple, pear, quince) in a pan with 2 tablespoons water and cinnamon for 5 minutes and let cool.
Whisk the yogurt with honey or grape molasses until smooth.
Lightly toast the oats in a dry pan for 2–3 minutes and let cool.
Put a spoonful of oats in the bottom of 4 glasses, then yogurt, then fruit; repeat the layers once more.
Sprinkle with walnuts and chill in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
Use strained yogurt so juicy fruit (strawberry, peach) doesn’t make it watery.
If you add the oats just before serving, they stay crunchy.
Serve cold; fresh mint leaves suit it well.
Keeps covered in the fridge for 1 day.
Warm vegetable salad with green lentils
2 cups chopped vegetables (zucchini, eggplant, cauliflower, broccoli, carrot or mushroom)
Wash the lentils and boil in plenty of water for 20–25 minutes so they stay firm; drain.
Sauté the vegetables in 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium-high heat for 8–10 minutes until golden at the edges.
Slice the red onion thinly.
Whisk the remaining olive oil, pomegranate molasses, cumin and salt to make a dressing.
Toss the warm lentils, vegetables, onion and chopped parsley with the dressing.
Don’t overboil the lentils or the salad turns mushy.
The dressing soaks into warm lentils better.
Serve lukewarm; crumbled white cheese can be added on top.
Vegetables with rice in olive oil
3 cups chopped vegetables (zucchini, eggplant, cauliflower, broccoli, leek, celeriac or carrot)
1 dessert spoon salt, 1 teaspoon sugar
Fry the onion in olive oil for 4 minutes.
Add the vegetables and stir for 5 minutes.
Add the chopped tomato, washed rice, salt and sugar.
Add the hot water and cook over low heat for 25 minutes.
Squeeze lemon over and leave to cool in the pot.
Olive-oil dishes are served lukewarm or cold.
Serve cold with yogurt.
